standard_prerequisites.name: Characterisation of computability by c.e. of a set and its complement
standard_prerequisites.use: Second claim: c.e.-ness of A and its complement, obtained from B's computability through the reduction, yields computability of A.

core_obligations: Statement (lines 1842-1849): if A <=_m B then (1) B c.e. implies A c.e.; (2) B computable implies A computable.
Claim (1) (proof lines 1851-1860): with f the reduction and B = dom(g), A = dom(g after f); the iff chain x in A iff f(x) in B iff g(f(x)) converges is displayed.

Claim (2) (lines 1861-1868): f is also a reduction of complement A to complement B; both become c.e. by claim (1); thm:ce-comp closes to computability (with the characteristic-function alternative noted by the author).
proof_roadmap: Unfold the reduction along domains for claim (1).
Transport the reduction to complements and invoke the characterisation for claim (2).
difficulty_reason: Closure properties of many-one reductions (statement 1842-1849, proof 1851-1868): two short but complete arguments, the second composed with the c.e.-characterisation stub. H2.
